Hi Elena —

I pulled together the technical definitions requested and attached a short SLO-Definitions.md. High-level answers below (happy to expand line-by-line against the Excel):

- Availability definition: We define a request as "failed" when the service returns any 5xx or when the request exceeds a hard timeout (default 30s). Network-level connection failures and closed TCP sessions are also counted as failures for availability SLOs. We exclude client-side timeouts attributable to client misconfiguration.

- Measurement unit: Per-request evaluation aggregated to 1-minute buckets across the region(s) you use, then rolled up to calendar-month for SLA reporting. The reported uptime = 1 - (failed_requests / total_requests) over the chosen window.

- Latency: We compute p50/p90/p95/p99 on end-to-end request latency (time from request ingress at our edge to final token emitted). For very short-lived requests we also report median and p99.9 on demand. Latency percentiles are computed on the same 1-minute buckets and then combined using weighted aggregation to preserve percentile characteristics.

- Sampling: By default we measure 100% of production traffic for availability and latency percentiles. For extremely high-volume customers we provide a configurable sampling policy but only if requested; sampling policies are documented and applied consistently.

- Synthetic checks: We run synthetic health probes every 30s across regions. Synthetic checks feed an independent availability signal used for platform-level alerts (not billing) and are included in incident reviews.

- Error budget & exceptions: Error budgets are tracked on a rolling 30-day and calendar-month basis. For scheduled maintenance windows we offer two options: (1) pre-agreed maintenance windows that are exempt from SLA calculations if scheduled >72h in advance and posted to the status page; (2) emergency maintenance which we evaluate for credit eligibility after post-incident review. Non-Redwood third-party platform outages (e.g., cloud provider outages) are treated per the standard force-majeure section but we provide detailed logs for audits.

Attachment: SLO-Definitions.md

If you want, I can produce an export of 3 months of sample metrics from our staging environment to show calculation mechanics.

—Karthik

- Traces/logs: Read-only access to traces is available with RBAC; full raw logs can be forwarded to your cloud storage or SIEM for retention.
- Compliance docs: SOC 2 report and recent penetration-test summary available; will attach SOC2-report-redwood.pdf to the final packet.

Elena —

Consolidating the answers from engineering and reliability:

1) SLA baseline: For Dedicated deployments our standard SLA is 99.95% monthly availability; for Hosted customers we publish a 99.9% baseline with higher tiers available by contract.
2) Measurement and reporting: Calendar-month for billing and SLA credits; rolling 30-day for operational dashboards. We will provide the CSV/Prometheus export for the months requested and a sample calculation workbook.
3) Alerts & access: We will provision a read-only console project with Grafana dashboards and an Ops webhook template for PagerDuty. If BrightEdge wants us to send platform alerts into your PD schedule, we can set that as part of the onboarding checklist.
4) Exceptions: Maintenance windows scheduled >72 hours in advance will be excluded from SLA calculations if agreed in writing. For unexpected platform events, we will run a post-incident review and recommend credit adjustments per the standard SLA exhibit; these are handled case-by-case.

Next steps I propose:
- I will fill your Excel with the responses above and return it by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule a 30-minute technical review — Karthik and Marissa are available Wednesday (Feb 11) 10:00–12:00 PT or Thursday 14:00–16:00 PT.
- If procurement is ready, I can generate the Exhibit A (SLA) DocuSign and include the monitoring access checklist.

Let me know which time works for your SREs and procurement.

Best,
Camila
